memos.headline: NVDA and MSFT at 52-week highs with overbought RSI; AAPL and UNH remain structurally weak
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe as of June 27. NVDA (+43% over 12 weeks, RSI 76.6) and MSFT (+30% over 12 weeks, RSI 77.0) are sitting right at their 52-week highs with massive relative strength versus SPY, but both are stretched more than 11% above their 50-day means and overbought on RSI—momentum is undeniable yet the risk of a mean-reversion pullback is elevated. AMZN at 223.30 looks like the cleanest setup: strong 12-week relative strength (+6.6% vs SPY), RSI at a healthy 67.9, and still 7.8% off its high, giving room to run without the same overbought risk. On the weak side, AAPL is 22% off its high, 10% below its 200-day mean, and showing -19.5% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks—a clear downtrend I would not fight. UNH at -50.6% drawdown and -37.7% below its 200-day mean is in freefall territory; the slight bounce over the past four weeks (+3.7%) is unconvincing given the magnitude of the decline.

Near all-time highs with RSI 77 and +20.1% 12w relative strength, but +11.3% above 50d mean signals stretch; a close below 460 would change my view.

memos.headline: Mega-cap tech earnings power dominates; CAT and XOM face margin compression
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in MSFT, NVDA, and GOOGL, all posting double-digit revenue growth with net margins north of 36%. MSFT delivered $70.1B revenue (+13.3% YoY) at a 36.9% net margin with manageable $42.9B debt, while GOOGL printed $90.2B revenue (+12.0%) at an extraordinary 38.3% margin on just $14.8B of debt—the cleanest balance sheet in the group relative to earnings. NVDA's 69.2% revenue growth and 42.6% net margin are remarkable, though I note net income growth of 26.2% lagged revenue growth meaningfully, suggesting some cost pressure worth monitoring. On the other end, CAT's revenue declined 9.8% with net income down 29.8%, and XOM posted flat revenue with a 6.2% net income decline—both showing operating leverage working against them. UNH's unavailable YoY net income comparison and thin 5.7% margin on $81.3B of debt make me cautious until I see clearer earnings trajectory.

views.note: 13.3% revenue growth, 36.9% net margin, and 17.7% net income growth on moderate $42.9B debt signals durable earnings power.
38.3% net margin with 46% net income growth and only $14.8B debt is the best margin-leverage combination in the universe.
69.2% revenue growth and 42.6% margin are exceptional, but the gap between revenue and net income growth (26.2%) flags rising costs that could compress margins.
Net income surged 64.2% YoY to $17.1B on 8.6% revenue growth, lifting margin to 11.0%—I'd revisit if margin expansion stalls below 10%.
Revenue +5.1% and net income +4.8% are steady but unexciting against $92.2B of total debt; I need to see services mix accelerate to get more constructive.
Solid 32.3% net margin and 9.1% earnings growth, but the bank's $407B debt load means credit cycle risk dominates the fundamental picture.
Revenue down 9.8% and net income down 29.8% show severe operating deleverage; I'd need a revenue inflection before reconsidering.
Flat revenue (+0.1%) and a 6.2% net income decline on a 9.3% margin leave no margin of safety if commodity prices weaken further.
5.7% net margin on $81.3B debt with unavailable YoY net income data is a red flag; I need clarity on earnings trajectory before engaging.
Revenue declined 2.1% with net income barely positive at +0.4%; stable 19.1% margin is defensive but I see no catalyst for earnings acceleration.

memos.headline: Fed Pausing at 4.50% With Cooling Labor Market and Benign Inflation Favors Duration-Sensitive Growth Over Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has held at 4.50% for three months while the effective rate sits at 4.33%, unchanged over the same window. CPI is running at just +2.4% y/y, close enough to target that the next move is more likely a cut than a hike, especially with unemployment drifting up to 4.3% (+40bp y/y). The 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply to +56bp (up 95bp over 12 months), confirming the curve has fully un-inverted—a classic late-pause/early-easing signal. I have moderate conviction that this regime favors long-duration growth names and defensive staples while arguing for caution on cyclicals and energy exposed to a softening demand backdrop; a surprise CPI print above 3% or a payrolls surge reversing the unemployment trend would force me to revisit.

views.note: High-quality duration asset benefits from stable-to-falling long rates and a steepening curve in a pause-to-easing regime.
Benign 2.4% CPI and a Fed on hold support equity multiples for mega-cap growth with strong cash flows.
Duration-sensitive secular grower stands to benefit if the next rate move is a cut, though elevated valuation tempers confidence.
Defensive staple with bond-proxy characteristics is attractive as unemployment rises and the curve steepens toward easing.
Steeper curve helps NIM but rising unemployment and potential credit deterioration offset; net neutral until labor data clarifies.
Consumer-facing growth name benefits from cooling inflation preserving real spending power and a supportive rate backdrop.
Cyclical bellwether faces headwinds from softening labor market and a macro regime tilting toward slowdown rather than expansion.
Energy demand outlook weakens as unemployment trends higher; restrictive policy still in place limits upside.
Ad-driven growth benefits from stable rates and benign inflation; steepening curve historically supportive for growth multiples.
Defensive healthcare name is macro-insensitive; no strong directional call from current rate and inflation data.

memos.headline: UNH Leadership Churn Dominates Narrative Risk; NVDA Post-Earnings Tone Already Absorbed
memos.body: I am reading the 8-K filing cadence and event types across the universe as a proxy for narrative intensity, since I lack direct GDELT tone scores in this evidence set. UNH stands out with four 8-K filings since mid-May, three of which involve officer departures/appointments—an unusually high rate of leadership turnover that typically generates negative media tone and headline risk, and the June 20 'Other Events' filing suggests the story is still evolving. NVDA's Q1 results 8-K on May 28 drew a +3.2% next-day price reaction, indicating the positive tone was quickly priced; I see limited further sentiment upside from that catalyst alone. PG's back-to-back filings in early June—a Deutsche Bank presentation and an officer announcement—suggest the company is actively managing its narrative, which I read as neutral-to-slightly-positive tone management. XOM's earnings reaction was a muted +0.4%, and subsequent filings are routine, leaving sentiment flat.

views.note: Three officer departure/appointment 8-Ks in six weeks signals leadership instability likely generating persistently negative media tone.
The +3.2% post-earnings pop on May 29 suggests positive sentiment was rapidly absorbed; no incremental tone catalyst visible.
Active investor-day and leadership communications in early June suggest proactive narrative management, mildly positive for tone trajectory.
Muted +0.4% earnings reaction and only routine shareholder-vote filing since; sentiment appears flat with no directional shift.
Reg FD disclosure and routine shareholder vote filings are low-signal; no tone inflection detected.
Two filings including Reg FD disclosure are standard cadence; insufficient evidence of a sentiment shift.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Falling Fast but Structural Tech-Supply-Chain and Energy Risks Persist
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has dropped 24% over three months to 239.86, and VIX is down to 16.59 (−19% m/m), suggesting markets are pricing out near-term policy shocks—but the absolute level of uncertainty remains elevated historically. HY spreads at 3.04% (−36 bps m/m) confirm risk appetite is recovering, yet WTI at $66.44 (−5.2% q/q) signals soft global demand or easing supply fears, which cuts both ways for energy names and tariff-sensitive industrials. I have moderate conviction that NVDA and AAPL remain structurally exposed to any escalation in US-China export controls or supply-chain disruptions, while CAT faces tariff and infrastructure-spending policy risk given its two recent 8-K filings in quick succession. XOM benefits from a relatively benign geopolitical energy premium at current crude levels, but I lack conviction that this calm persists if Middle East or Russia-related sanctions tighten.

views.note: Export-control risk to China remains a structural overhang despite easing near-term policy uncertainty; any tightening of chip restrictions would be material.
Supply-chain concentration in China and India transition keeps geopolitical tail risk alive even as broad uncertainty recedes; 8-K on 5/12 lacked detail to shift my view.
Two 8-K filings in a month and tariff/infrastructure policy sensitivity make CAT vulnerable if trade tensions re-escalate; WTI weakness also dampens mining capex outlook.
WTI at $66 reflects muted geopolitical energy premium; benign for margins now but any sanctions escalation on Russia or Iran could whipsaw crude higher.
Steepening yield curve (+19 bps 3m) and tightening HY spreads favor bank earnings; policy uncertainty decline reduces tail risk to credit quality.
Defensive staples benefit from residual policy uncertainty at 240; two recent Reg FD disclosures suggest proactive investor communication amid tariff-cost pass-through.
